434:  *
435:  * This way, the [block] gets cancelled when either the caller or `scopeWithTheRequiredJob` gets cancelled,
436:  * ensuring that unnecessary computations do not keep executing.
437:  *
438:  * ## Dispatching behavior
439:  *
440:  * If [context] provides a [ContinuationInterceptor] other than the one used by the caller,
441:  * the [block] cannot simply be called inline with the updated context and has to go through a dispatch,
442:  * that is, get scheduled on the new [ContinuationInterceptor].
443:  * It is up to the [ContinuationInterceptor] to actually run the [block],
444:  * and it may take arbitrarily long for that to happen.
445:  * After the [block] has completed, the computation has to be dispatched back to the original
446:  * [ContinuationInterceptor].
447:  *
448:  * If the resulting context in which [block] should run has the same [ContinuationInterceptor]
449:  * as the caller, no dispatch is performed.
450:  * In that case, no dispatch happens on exiting the [block] either, unless child coroutines have to be awaited.
451:  *
452:  * Note that the result of a [withContext] invocation is dispatched into the original context in a cancellable way
453:  * with a **prompt cancellation guarantee**, which means that if the original [currentCoroutineContext]
454:  * in which [withContext] was invoked is cancelled by the time its dispatcher starts to execute the code,
455:  * it discards the result of [withContext] and throws a [CancellationException].
456:  *
457:  * On the other hand, if the dispatch from [withContext] back to the original context does not need to happen
458:  * (because of having the same dispatcher and not having to wait for the children)
459:  * *and* the [context] passed to [withContext] contains [NonCancellable],
460:  * then cancellation of the caller will not prevent a value from being successfully returned.
461:  *
462:  * ## Pitfalls
463:  *
464:  * ### Returning closeable resources
465:  *
466:  * Values returned from [withContext] will typically be lost if the caller is cancelled.
467:  * An important exception is the `withContext(NonCancellable)` pattern.
468:  *
469:  * See the corresponding section in the [coroutineScope] documentation for details,
470:  * as well as the [NonCancellable] documentation.
471:  */
